outputs.explanation: This is a stacked area/bar chart showing median promoter-state frequencies across many continuous bins of Pol II ChIP-seq signal (n=5912 promoters). Functionally this behaves like a continuous stacked-area/line plot depicting a trend across an ordered continuous variable rather than a simple bar chart comparing discrete groups; overlaying thousands of individual promoter values onto a 100%-stacked composition across many fine bins would be unreadable and is not meaningful, similar to the line-plot exemption.

The single-molecule stack itself displays every individual DNA molecule (one row per molecule, 2952 molecules) with its own methylation pattern, so the raw individual data underlying the summarized state frequencies (shown in the adjacent color sidebar) are directly visualized.

Same representation as panel A (mouse data): a stacked area/bar chart of median state frequencies across continuous Pol II ChIP-seq bins (n=6122 promoters). As in A, this is analogous to a continuous trend plot where overlaying individual data points is not meaningful or readable.

Same representation as panel B for the mouse Skp1 locus: each row of the single-molecule stack (2871 molecules) shows an individual molecule's methylation pattern, so individual data underlying the summarized state frequencies are shown directly.

This is a box plot comparing PIC occupancy distributions across TATA-less/TATA-containing promoters in mouse and Drosophila. Box plots are exempt from requiring overlaid individual points since they already convey the distribution (median, IQR, whiskers).

This is a box plot comparing Pol II occupancy distributions across TATA-less/TATA-containing promoters in mouse and Drosophila. Box plots are exempt from requiring overlaid individual points since they already convey the distribution (median, IQR, whiskers).
